title: The Loose Protocol
premise: Gideon Vane, once the interpreter who mistranslated a single sentence during ceasefire talks and triggered a massacre he's spent years hiding from, works quietly as a document translator in Lisbon. When a dead colleague's voiceprint unlocks a hidden server, Gideon discovers 'The Loose Protocol': a false-flag attack engineered to look like an industrial accident, scheduled to destroy the fragile peace process he once broke. Pursued by the intelligence officer who covered up the original massacre and the mercenary cell executing the plan, Gideon must ally with Amara Diallo, the investigator hunting the truth about that night. In the end, Gideon publicly confesses his own role in the massacre to expose the conspiracy, stopping the attack at the cost of his anonymity, his freedom, and the last chance at the quiet life he built.
about_author: Elodie Quintana is a former conference interpreter turned novelist who spent a decade working behind the glass booths of international summits. She writes thrillers about the people history forgets were in the room.

chapters.title: The Glass Booth
chapters.summary: Gideon Vane, POV. Gideon translates insurance documents in Lisbon, a life deliberately too small to attract attention. A nightmare about a negotiation room establishes the insomnia and guilt he carries. Emotional beat: the suffocating safety of a man hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. A package arrives containing a dead colleague's dictaphone; playing it, Gideon hears his own voice reciting a passphrase that unlocks a remote server. He hesitates, then logs in. Emotional beat: dread curdling into fatal curiosity.

chapters.title: The Loose Protocol
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The server holds files on a planned chemical plant 'accident' in Geneva timed to collapse peace talks, plus a roster of names, including Gideon's. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing his invisibility was an illusion.

chapters.title: Amara
chapters.summary: Amara Diallo, POV. An investigator with the peace-monitoring mission, Amara is auditing anomalies in the delegation's security contracts. She notices the same plant and the same dates. Emotional beat: professional unease sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. A gray-eyed stranger appears outside Gideon's building; his flat has been searched but nothing taken. Gideon burns his notes. Emotional beat: paranoia becoming physical, the past knocking at the door.

chapters.title: Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara interviews survivors of the Kesswil incident, the massacre that ended the last peace process, and finds the official record contradicts testimony. A translator's name is redacted. Emotional beat: the pull of a story she isn't supposed to want.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The colleague who sent the dictaphone is reported dead in a fall. Gideon recognizes staging when he sees it. He decides to run, then decides instead to dig. Emotional beat: grief converting to resolve.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Gideon, POV. Eight years ago: the negotiation, the pressure, the sentence Gideon softened under instruction, and the attack that followed. Emotional beat: the origin of his guilt and his belief that words kill.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon anonymously tips Amara's office, then panics and tries to retract it. She traces the call anyway and shows up at his door. Emotional beat: the terror and relief of being seen.

chapters.title: Two Liars
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Gideon gives Amara partial truths, omitting Kesswil. She catches the omission but hides that she caught it. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: two people negotiating trust like a hostage exchange.

chapters.title: The Roster
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Decoding the server roster, Gideon identifies the mercenary cell's logistics chief, a man he once interpreted for. He realizes he is not just a witness but an intended scapegoat. Emotional beat: hunted prey realizing it was always on the menu.

chapters.title: Geneva Bound
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara requests transfer to the Geneva delegation, citing audit irregularities. Her supervisor, Halvard, approves too quickly. Emotional beat: the cold realization that someone wants her close, or gone.

chapters.title: Train to the Alps
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon travels to Geneva under a false name; the gray-eyed man is on the train. A near-encounter in the dining car. Emotional beat: the hunter's patience, the prey's discipline.

chapters.title: The Plant
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara tours the chemical facility under audit pretext and photographs a secondary pipeline that matches the server schematics. Emotional beat: proof turning abstract dread into concrete architecture.

chapters.title: Halvard
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara confronts her supervisor with the pipeline photos; he warns her off with a veiled reference to Kesswil and careers that ended there. Emotional beat: institutional menace, the machine defending itself.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon and Amara finally compare notes in a lakeside safehouse. He confesses the softened sentence; she reveals her brother died at Kesswil. Emotional beat: the fragile, painful birth of real trust.

chapters.title: The Gray-Eyed Man
chapters.summary: The gray-eyed man (Kessler), POV. Kessler, the intelligence officer who orchestrated the Kesswil cover-up, reports to his handler that Vane is in Geneva. We learn the Protocol's architect is inside the peace mission itself. Emotional beat: the banality of a true believer.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Decrypted scheduling files reveal the attack window: eleven days. Gideon proposes going to the delegation; Amara argues Halvard can't be trusted. Emotional beat: time pressure fracturing their strategy.

chapters.title: The Whistle That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara's formal report is buried within hours; her access is revoked. She realizes she is now officially a problem. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being erased by paperwork.

chapters.title: Old Contacts
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon reaches out to a retired interpreter, Marta, who kept records from Kesswil. She agrees to meet. Emotional beat: hope, and the guilt of endangering an old friend.

chapters.title: Marta
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Marta's archive shows the softened sentence was dictated from above, by Kessler. Gideon wasn't the author of the massacre, only its instrument. Emotional beat: guilt reframed, not relieved.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Café
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The meeting is compromised; Kessler's men take Marta and the archive. Gideon escapes with one stolen page. Emotional beat: survivor's shame, the price of every choice.

chapters.title: The Page
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. The stolen page names the Protocol's inside man: not Halvard, but the delegation's own security chief, Brenner. Emotional beat: the map of the conspiracy suddenly legible.

chapters.title: Brenner's Offer
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Brenner corners Gideon, offering immunity and a new identity if he disappears and lets the attack happen. Gideon pretends to consider. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara, tailing Brenner, is nearly killed in a staged hit-and-run; Gideon pulls her from the road. Emotional beat: loyalty proven in blood, the cost of staying in the game.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon remembers the dictaphone holds a second track: Kessler's voice, giving the instruction at Kesswil. They have the confession, but playing it exposes Gideon too. Emotional beat: truth and self-destruction bound together.

chapters.title: Split Decision
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara wants to broadcast the recording immediately; Gideon argues they need Brenner's operational files first to actually stop the attack. They quarrel and split tasks. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth, the theme made explicit.

chapters.title: Into the Server Room
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon uses his old interpreter credentials to infiltrate the delegation's annex and copies Brenner's operational drive. Kessler nearly catches him. Emotional beat: the invisible man learning to move in the light.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. The drive confirms the attack method and reveals a second target: the signing ceremony itself. The 'accident' is meant to kill the negotiators. Emotional beat: stakes doubling, the floor dropping out.

chapters.title: Marta's Silence
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. News arrives that Marta died in custody. Gideon breaks; Amara holds the line. He resolves to stop hiding. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into the decision to confess publicly.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Gideon and Amara alternate POV. With two days left, they plan a three-front move: warn the negotiators, trigger the plant's safety shutdown, and broadcast the recording. Emotional beat: grim clarity, the calm of no options left.

chapters.title: Kessler's Trap
chapters.summary: Kessler, POV. Kessler anticipates them, using the delegation's channels to brand Amara and Gideon as terrorists. The trap is set at the plant. Emotional beat: the antagonist's cold confidence.

chapters.title: The Warning
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara reaches the head negotiator directly, risking arrest, and convinces her to delay the ceremony. Half the plan succeeds. Emotional beat: one honest voice against a machine.

chapters.title: Shutdown
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon enters the plant to trip the safety systems manually; Brenner confronts him. A brutal, quiet fight; Gideon wins by knowing the facility's language, literally reading the German control labels. Emotional beat: his old skills weaponized.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara releases the Kesswil recording to press and delegations worldwide, including Gideon's own softened sentence, unedited and unexplained. Emotional beat: truth as a grenade with no friendly shrapnel.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The attack triggers early and fails, contained by the shutdown; the cell scatters. Kessler, exposed, tries to flee through the plant. Gideon confronts him in the control room. Emotional beat: the past and present colliding in one room.

chapters.title: Kesswil, Again
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon forces Kessler to hear his own voice from the recording, then holds him for arriving monitors rather than taking revenge. Emotional beat: choosing justice over the massacre's logic.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon gives a full public statement: his role at Kesswil, the coercion, the cover-up. The peace process, paradoxically, survives on the credibility of radical honesty. Emotional beat: the price paid, and paid willingly.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Kessler and Brenner are indicted; Gideon accepts a reduced sentence for cooperation. Amara visits him; something unspoken and unromanticized passes between them. Emotional beat: loyalty outlasting the case.

chapters.title: The First Night
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Months later, in an open prison near the lake, Gideon sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. He wakes to ordinary light. Emotional beat: belonging found not in invisibility, but in accountability.
